minutes.headline: ZBA approved an auto sales/repair special permit and a shed accessory-use appeal; Pond View water/sewer authority was continued.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard two applications and a continued 40B hearing. It granted a special permit for auto repair and sales at 383 Whalum Road with conditions, and granted the Richards Way shed appeal on condition it be removed if the lots are sold separately. On the Pond View Commons 40B, members signaled by informal straw poll that they lack authority to waive water and sewer requirements. Town counsel will draft a stipulation to take the question to the Housing Appeals Committee, and the hearing was continued to February 8.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment on the auto sales application; no one spoke.
Supports the shed; said he is the one neighbor who can see it.
Asked whether the planning board step was waived; said she has no problem with the shed and agrees with the zoning rationale.
Supports the shed and thanked the board.
A resident wanted the shed gone from 10 Richards Way whenever the property is sold, even to a child.
A resident from Maysville Road asked how the shed removal would be enforced in the future.

public_comment.stated_role: chairman of the board of water commissioners
public_comment.topic: Read and summarized counsel's letter: the water district cannot sell water outside its bounds and neither the ZBA nor the HAC can override the district vote; the district voted against negotiating.

votes.motion: Grant special permit for auto repair and auto sales with 30 vehicles, a six foot setback from Route 13, a clear corner at the Whalum Road entrance, and police and fire access check before planning board.
votes.outcome: passed (individual ayes heard; full count not clearly audible)

votes.motion: Grant the appeal so the shed at 10 Richards Way is an accessory use to the residence at 8 Richards Way, must be removed or resolved if the lots are sold separately, and 10 Richards Way is a non-conforming lot while the shed is there.
votes.outcome: passed (ayes heard; full count not audible)

votes.motion: Continue the Pond View Commons hearing to February 8 at seven o'clock.

budget_items.what_was_said: The applicant funded a traffic peer review but declined to fund an engineering review until the water and sewer authority question is settled; funding would be committed if the ZBA is found to have authority.

decisions.decision: By informal straw poll, members indicated they support taking the water/sewer authority question to the Housing Appeals Committee; town counsel was authorized to draft and negotiate a stipulation, with no formal vote yet.
Counsel will bring a draft stipulation, including a board vote that it lacks authority to waive the water and sewer requirements, to the next meeting.
Pond View hearing continued to February 8 at seven o'clock.
Auto-sales conditions set, including no display cars between the Whalum Road entrance and the first telephone pole, and hours Monday to Friday eight to five.

what_happened.line: The board granted a special permit for auto repair and auto sales at 383 Whalum Road, with conditions on vehicle count, setback, hours and access.
The board granted the Richards Way appeal, treating the shed at 10 Richards Way as an accessory use, to be removed or resolved if the lots are sold separately.
On the Pond View Commons 40B, members indicated by informal straw poll, with no formal vote, that they support taking the water and sewer question to the Housing Appeals Committee.
Town counsel will bring a draft stipulation, including a board vote that it lacks authority to waive water and sewer requirements, to the next meeting.
The Pond View hearing was continued to February 8 at seven o'clock by unanimous voice vote.

why_it_matters: The Whalum Road permit sets enforceable operating conditions for a commercial use on Route 13, and the Richards Way ruling sets a removal condition that neighbors asked how the town would enforce.
The Pond View 40B turns on whether the town or the water district controls water and sewer service for the project, a question the Housing Appeals Committee may end up deciding.
